description: The time hierarchy consists of Year, Quarter, Month, Week End Date, and Reporting Date. This field can be used in reporting to drill up or down to the level of analysis needed.
The customer day of week refers to the day of sales.

The customer month is specific to a customer's calendar and reporting period. Customers either utilize a 4-4-5 or a 4-5-4 weekly period for their monthly aggregations. Depending on the customer, February may include different weeks for one customer than another.
The customer month is specific to a customer's calendar and reporting period. It is the numeric representation of the customer's month.
The customer month year is specific to a customer's calendar and reporting period. The customer month year takes into consideration how a customer groups together their week, month, and year.

The customer month year is specific to a customer's calendar and reporting period. The customer quarter will vary as each customer's fiscal period begins at different times. For example, Walmart's Q1 is Feb - Apr. Walgreen's Q1 is Sept - Nov.
This is the abbreviation of the Customer Quarter field.
This is the numeric representation of the Customer Quarter field.

The customer time hierarchy consists of Customer Year, Customer Quarter, Customer Month, Customer Week End Date, and Reporting Date. This field can be used in reporting to drill up or down to the level of analysis needed.

A customer's week end date is specific to their calendar and reporting period. This field is based on the Customer Calendar selected. For example, Costco's week runs Monday - Sunday. Therefore, you'd have to select a week ending date that lands on a Sunday if using the customer's calendar. Data would then show for Sunday - Monday.

A customer's week number is specific to their calendar and reporting period. This field is based on the Customer Calendar selected. For example, Walmart's year starts in Feb. Therefore, their week 1 would begin in Feb. Depending on the customer calendar chosen, the week number may start at different points in time.

A customer's year is specific to their calendar and reporting period. This field is based on the Customer Calendar selected. For example, Walmart's calendar year runs February - January. By selecting 2025 and the Walmart Customer  Calendar, data would show for Feb 2025 - Jan 2026 data.

A customer's year is specific to their calendar and reporting period. This field is based on the Customer Calendar selected. Depending on the customer, the year and month will have different dates that fall into that grouping.

A customer's year is specific to their calendar and reporting period. This field is based on the Customer Calendar selected. Depending on the customer, the year and week will have different dates that fall into that grouping.
Useful for viewing by day, ex: "Monday", "Tuesday", etc.

Useful for grouping by month name, ex. "April". Month will be defined by the default or based on a filter selected in the Calendar Type dimension. For example, January for Invoice Sales or Standard Calendar is Jan 1 - Jan 31. January for POS Sales or the Retail Calendar is Week 1 - Week 4.

Useful for grouping by month name abbreviated, "ex. Apr". Month will be defined by the default or based on a filter selected in the Calendar Type dimension. For example, January for Invoice Sales or Standard Calendar is Jan 1 - Jan 31. January for POS Sales or the Retail Calendar is Week 1 - Week 4.

Useful for grouping by month number, ex. "4". Month will be defined by the default or based on a filter selected in the Calendar Type dimension. For example, January for Invoice Sales or Standard Calendar is Jan 1 - Jan 31. January for POS Sales or the Retail Calendar is Week 1 - Week 4.

Useful for grouping by month abbreviated and year, ex. "April 2021". Month will be defined by the default or based on a filter selected in the Calendar Type dimension. For example, January for Invoice Sales or Standard Calendar is Jan 1 - Jan 31. January for POS Sales or the Retail Calendar is Week 1 - Week 4.

Useful for grouping by quarter, ex. "Quarter 2". Quarter will be defined by the default or based on a filter selected in the Calendar Type dimension. For example, Quarter 1 for Invoice Sales or Standard Calendar is Jan 1 - Mar 31. Quarter 1 for POS Sales or the Retail Calendar is Week 1 - Week 13.

Useful for grouping by quarter, ex. "Q2". Quarter will be defined by the default or based on a filter selected in the Calendar Type dimension. For example, Quarter 1 for Invoice Sales or Standard Calendar is Jan 1 - Mar 31. Quarter 1 for POS Sales or the Retail Calendar is Week 1 - Week 13.
Useful for grouping by Quarter based on standard calendar from Jan 1-Dec 31, ex: "Quarter 1", "Quarter 2", etc.

Useful for grouping by quarter, ex. "Q2 2021". Quarter will be defined by the default or based on a filter selected in the Calendar Type dimension. For example, Quarter 1 for Invoice Sales or Standard Calendar is Jan 1 - Mar 31. Quarter 1 for POS Sales or the Retail Calendar is Week 1 - Week 13.

Date of transaction. Reporting Date definition may change depending on the fact selected. Sales-related Facts: Reporting Date is the date of the transaction. Open Order Facts: Reporting Date is the expected ship date. Order Intake Facts: Reporting Date is the Created On Date for Sales Document.
Useful for grouping by week based on the 445 Calendar from Jan-Dec with Saturday Weekending, ex "4/17/2021",  "4/24/2021", etc.
Concatenated YYYY?MMM formatted representation of the calendar period, used in reporting for grouping by month.

Useful for grouping by year and month number, ex. "202104". Month will be defined by the default or based on a filter selected in the Calendar Type dimension. Useful for grouping by year and week number based on the 445 Calendar from Jan-Dec with Saturday Weekending, ex "202115".

description: Time Periods are pre-baked collections of dates that can be used with most facts. Time Periods will always default to look backwards from the most recent refresh of data. Time Period will be defined by the default or based on a filter selected in the Calendar Type dimension. For example, YTD for Invoice Sales or Standard Calendar will include Jan 1 - Dec 31. YTD for POS Sales or the Retail Calendar will include Week 1 - Week 52.

crossSystemEquivalents.Oracle OBIEE: Time Period

description: Numeric date key equivalent.

Time Periods can be used with Anchor Date, Anchor Month, Anchor Month Number, and Anchor Week End Date if a user wants to create a specific “as of” time period. Example: If Last Week is used with an Anchor Week End Date of 6/5/2021 then the Last Week would aggregate sales for 5/30/2021 – 6/5/2021. Anchor Date definition may change depending on the fact selected. Snapshot Facts: Anchor Date is the date the snapshot was taken. Example: Open Orders Snapshot with an Anchor Date selection of 6/7/2021, the data represents what Open Orders were on 6/7/2021. Non-Snapshot Facts: Anchor Date is the last date of transactions included in the time period selected. Example: Invoice Sales with an Anchor Date selection of 6/7/2021, the data represents what shipped on or before 6/7/2021 for the time period selected.
